questions.question: Q: State the three main principles of stratigraphy.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Superposition: oldest beds at the bottom. 2) Original horizontality: beds are deposited horizontally. 3) Cross-cutting relationships: a feature that cuts another is younger.

questions.question: Q: What makes a good index fossil?
questions.correctAnswer: Short geological time range (rapid evolution), wide geographical distribution, easily recognisable, and abundant in the rock record.

questions.question: Q: How does radiometric dating work?
questions.correctAnswer: A radioactive parent isotope decays into a stable daughter isotope at a known rate (half-life). By measuring the ratio of parent to daughter isotopes in a mineral, the age since the mineral crystallised (its closure temperature) can be calculated.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between relative and absolute dating?
questions.correctAnswer: Relative dating places rocks in chronological order (older/younger) without giving numerical ages. Absolute (radiometric) dating measures the actual age in years (typically millions of years) using radioactive isotope decay.
